items.body:
MEETING DATE:
9/15/2026
TOPIC:
Approve the Financial Report and Monthly Bills & Payroll for the Month Ended June 30, 2026
BACKGROUND:
The Finance Department prepares financial reports and a monthly bills & payroll report at the end of each
month. These reports summarize the financial activities of the school division. The reports prepared include:
1. Financial Highlights
2. Budget Status Report – All Funds
3. Expenditures by Cost Center – Operating Fund
4. Monthly Bills & Payroll – All Funds
5. Purchase Orders issued over $25,000
6. Contracts Signed between $25,000 - $100,000
7. Transfers Between Categories up to $25,000
RATIONALE:
The presentation of the monthly financial reports and monthly bills & payroll report ensures accountability to
the board and the citizens of James City County and the City of Williamsburg of the financial resources
entrusted to the school division.

items.title: Approval of Resolution R-19-26, Bullying Prevention Month
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
9/15/2026
TOPIC:
Approve Resolution R-19-26, Bullying Prevention Month
POLICY ALIGNMENT:
JFC, Student Conduct
BACKGROUND:
To promote awareness of school bullying, the Virginia School Boards Association of Directors has set aside
the month of October as Bullying Prevention Awareness Month.
RATIONALE:
Childhood bullying is a significant problem nationwide. It can cause school absenteeism, mental and physical
stress, poor school performance, and poor self-esteem. School board members, superintendents, teachers,
and parents can play a critical role in creating a climate where bullying is not tolerated. Each October, WJCC
Public Schools supports Bullying Prevention Month through a variety of activities. The division website is
utilized to provide information on bullying prevention and the October observance. Each school plans specific
activities to acknowledge Bullying Prevention Month.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends that the board approve Resolution R-19-26, declaring the month of October
2026 as Bullying Prevention Month in the Williamsburg-James City County Public Schools.
DATA SOURCE:
Adam Brown, Ed.D., Chief Operating Officer
Nick Kier, Supervisor of Student Services and Interventions
RECOMMENDED ACTION:
Move to approve the consent agenda as presented.

items.title: Approval of Resolution R-20-26, National School Lunch Week
items.body:
MEETIN DATE:
9/15/2026
TOPIC:
Approve Resolution R-20-26, National School Lunch Week
BACKGROUND:
First declared in 1962, the annual observance of National School Lunch Week promotes the importance of a
healthy school lunch in a child's life and the impact it has inside and outside of the classroom.
The National School Lunch Program (NSLP) serves nearly 30 million children every school day to ensure the
health and well-being of all public school students, boost academic performance by giving students the fuel
they need to succeed, and closed the opportunity gap for children across the country. The program reduces
childhood hunger and also supports American agriculture.
RATIONALE:
The WJCC Child Nutrition Services Program provides lunch and breakfast to students daily, while adhering to
strict nutrition standards and navigating student food allergies. Research demonstrates a strong relationship
between nutrition and readiness to learn. The meals served to students provide the energy and nutrients for
optimal cognitive development and performance. Williamsburg-James City County has exceptional Child
Nutrition Services staff members in each of the sixteen schools, and the division is proud to recognize the
difference school nutrition professionals make for every child who comes through the cafeteria.
The week of October 12-16, 2026, is recognized as National School Lunch Week.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends that the board approve Resolution R-20-26 declaring the week of October
12-16, 2026, as National School Lunch Week in Williamsburg-James City County Schools.
DATA SOURCE:
Marcellus Snipes, Senior Director of Operations
Narong Wayne Cadwallader, Supervisor of Child Nutrition Services
RECOMMENDED ACTION:

items.title: Approval of the Fiscal Year 2026 Year-End Financial Report and Proposed Commitments of Fund Balance
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
9/15/2026
TOPIC:
Approve the Fiscal Year 2026 Year-End Financial Report and Proposed Commitment of Fund Balance
BACKGROUND:
Pursuant to Virginia Code § 22.1-100, WJCC Schools may not carry forward unexpended funds from one fiscal
year to the next unless the School Board takes action to commit or assign those funds for a specific purpose.
Historically, pursuant to the School Division’s operational contract with the City of Williamsburg and James City
County, 90% of unexpended funds were allocated to the “Future School Use Account”, with the remaining 10%
returned to the localities based on their respective funding shares.
During Fiscal Year 2026, James City County returned a portion of the School Division's Fiscal Year 2025 fund
balance to establish a healthcare reserve fund. Subsequently, both James City County and the City of
Williamsburg expressed support for directing any remaining Fiscal Year 2026 year-end fund balance to the
healthcare reserve fund to help address future healthcare cost obligations and strengthen the Division's longterm financial position.
RATIONALE:
Administration is recommending that the Fiscal Year 2026 year-end fund balance be committed to the
healthcare reserve fund. This recommendation is supported by both James City County and the City of
Williamsburg and advances the School Division's efforts to build financial capacity to manage future
healthcare-related expenditures.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
Revenue and expenditure information presented is preliminary, unaudited, and subject to change.
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation to commit the Fiscal Year 2026 year-end fund balance to the
healthcare reserve fund.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board approve the Fiscal Year 2026 Year-End Financial Report and
proposed commitment of the year-end fund balance to the healthcare reserve fund.

items.title: Review Advisory Committee Appointments
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
9/15/2026
TOPIC:
Review 2026-2027 Advisory Committee Member Appointments
POLICY ALIGNMENT:
BCF, School Board Committees
BACKGROUND:
Each year the school board appoints citizens to be on School Board Advisory Committees: Special Education
and Career Ready (CTE). These committees act in an advisory capacity only. The school board will
determine the number of members to serve on any advisory committee and shall appoint the members of the
committee. Membership on committees shall be in accordance with state and federal laws and regulations and
reflects, whenever possible, the diversity of the community. Members of the WJCC Schools administrative
staff shall serve only as resource persons and liaisons to the advisory committees.
RATIONALE:
Board Policy BCF, School Board Committees, lists the operating procedures to govern the operations of
advisory committees, unless otherwise provided by the school board or by state or federal law or regulations.
Unless prohibited by federal or state law, a minimum of one school board member is appointed to each
committee to represent the board and serve as a consultant to the committee. An advisory committee
appointment term is two years. Members of an advisory committee may be appointed for a second
consecutive two-year term. Members are ineligible to serve for more than two consecutive terms.
Appointments to advisory committees will be made by the first October school board meeting of each year.
The school board may make additional appointments to an advisory committee during the school year. After
committees are formed, any additional applications received will be saved for review and consideration either
in the event of mid-year vacancies, or for possible appointment the following school year.

items.title: Superintendent's Recommendation for School Division Redistricting
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
9/15/2026
TOPIC:
Superintendent's Recommendation for School Division Redistricting
BACKGROUND:
Many school buildings in WJCC Schools, specifically at the elementary level, are at capacity. To accommodate
student population, eight of nine WJCC elementary schools have portable classrooms (trailers) on site. With the
anticipated August 2027 occupancy of two new pre-k centers, the school division must also consider the best and
most efficient way to utilize elementary space that will be available when pre-k students are located in the new pre-k
spaces as the current pre-k program is housed in five elementary schools. The shift will leave some elementary
spaces unoccupied while other spaces remain at or over capacity. Engaging in conversation on school zones also
allows the school division to consider boundaries, feeder pattern alignment, efficiencies and effective delivery at the
secondary level.
RATIONALE:
The Redistricting Steering Committee released draft attendance zone maps for each level on May 12, 2026, and
revisions were presented on August 4, 2026. Community members engaged in two feedback processes. The
Redistricting Steering Committee presented a final map recommendation to Dr. Keever on September 1, 2026.
Dr. Keever will present his recommendation for school division redistricting to the school board.
